summary: Canada Lookouts records a 1930 cupola cabin on the summit and a 1950 telephone upgrade; no source found on the site today.

facts.design: Cupola cabin on the summit (1930 entry)
facts.agency: Department of Lands and Mines (New Brunswick), named in the 1950 entry

events.note: First entry for the summit: a cupola cabin on the 1,462-foot summit. The source does not say when it was built.
Telephone line to the lookout station rebuilt from grounded to metallic circuit, per the Department of Lands and Mines 114th Annual Report.

notes_for_editor: Two thin sources. The Canada Lookouts page is the only history: a 1930 cupola cabin and a 1950 telephone upgrade, nothing on construction, staffing, fires or fate. The OpenStreetMap node is the only other record and was last edited over 13 years ago. The brief's status 'standing' is not confirmed by any source read, so no status key was written; please verify. The page gives the summit as 1,462 feet and does not say whether that is tower height or summit elevation; the story uses it only as summit height, converted to 446 m. The 1930 structure is called a cupola cabin, not a tower, so the record's kind 'tower' may need a look. Two WebSearch runs found nothing on a Mount Champlain fire tower in New Brunswick (results were Mount Carleton, Big Bald Mountain and an unrelated Champlain Lookout in Quebec). The OSM access tag (yes) is not used as a fact because the entry is old. Suggested checks: New Brunswick provincial archives and Department of Lands and Mines annual reports. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the OSM node sits at 45.4783380, -66.2348739 on its node page, but no coordinates for Mount Champlain were read, so the story does not say the node is on the same site; the New Brunswick placement rests on the 'NEW BRUNSWICK LOOKOUTS' heading of the Canada Lookouts page.
